Board 4: 18.5px against the button's 18.5px on the computer, 17px against 17px on the dark phone. Board 6: 20px against 17px on the computer, 19px against 16.5px on the phones. Each open line is 6px or 7px larger than its fallback line. (2) The fallback line and link are the smallest text in each box (12px to 12.5px), muted, the link underlined, all contrast 6.1:1 or more. (3) Navy band: the open line is in the computer box and in the dark phone, the only phone picture that reaches the box. (4) Squint test at half size: the open line reads first on every box and the fallback line recedes; before this pass the bulletin had it the other way round. (5) Pixel comparison against the before-r10 renders: no change above the box or in the light phones. Below the box, the computer column moves down only by the box's growth. No overflow, clipping or collision. Declared heights stay true (2350 and 2450). (6) No em or en dash in either file; no date, time or example word changed.

changed: No changes needed. I made no edits to either file because the revised boards passed every revision10 check when I checked them myself.

Check (1): 'Registration is open' sits above the button in every view that shows the box. It is as large as or larger than the button's words, and 5.5px to 7px larger than the fallback line. Board 4: computer 18.5 vs button 18.5 vs fallback 12.5; dark phone 17 vs 17 vs 12. Board 6: computer 20 vs 17 vs 12.5; dark phone 19 vs 16.5 vs 12. Every open line is weight 700.

Check (2): the fallback line and its link are the smallest text in each box (12px to 12.5px), in muted grey (#555c6b light, #a9adb6 or #a9adb5 dark). Each link is underlined on a 24px line. Contrast is 6.1:1 to 7.27:1.
Check (3): the navy band board (Newsletter-Tournament-6) now has the open line in its computer box and in its dark phone, the only phone picture that reaches the box.

Check (4): I looked at the half-size crops as on a phone. On both boards the open line reads first and the fallback line fades back; on the bulletin that is the reverse of the before render. This matches K's words: the open line is now easy to see, the fallback line is the quiet one, and the navy band look has the line.

Check (5): I compared pixels with renders of the before-r10 copies. Everything above each box and both light phones are identical. Below each computer box, the only differences come from content moving down by the box's growth (about 3px on board 4, 14px on board 6). The text is the same and the differences are only anti-aliasing. The dark phones show the same content shifted (board 4 by 40px, board 6 by 18px); the differences there are also only anti-aliasing, and the last footer line has clean space above the bottom bar. No overflow, clipping or collision. Box padding looks even (board 6 computer: 25px above the open line, 23px below the fallback).

Check (6): no em dash or en dash in either file. No example word, date, time or fee changed; the diff against before-r10 touches only the box's styles, the two new open-line elements and the dark-phone scroll offsets. The skeletons are untouched and every added element is closed.
unresolved: Both dark-phone pictures now show the email scrolled slightly differently so the new open line clears the Inbox bar: 40px further on board 4 (the .np-end.t-bot bottom offset) and 18px on board 6 (the .np-dark .np-end offsets). On board 4 this pushes the small rook end mark under the footer out of the picture. It is fully hidden, with no sliver showing. On board 6 the box's top border now tucks under the Inbox bar, as board 4's already did. Showing everything would mean changing spacing elsewhere, which this pass does not allow, so I left it as the designer set it.
The bulletin's open line is 18.5px, slightly above the spec's 'about 17px to 18px', because check (1) requires it to be at least as large as the button's words (18.5px).

Canvas sticky note: Registration box, both tournament send-outs. 'Registration is open' now comes first, as the box's heading above the button: 18.5px bold navy capitals on the bulletin, and 20px bold navy on the navy band look, which did not have this line before. It appears on the dark phone too, in white. 'If the button does not show, use this link:' and its link are now small, quiet grey text (12px to 12.5px) under the button, still underlined and easy to tap.
